set -u
# ac3 - THE BITE, MEASURED ON THROWAWAY FIXTURES ONLY. Read-only against the repository:
# every mutation happens on a COPY of the index inside a throwaway dir, so the tracked index
# is never at risk (and this card could not write it anyway - index ownership is t105's).
# Three behaviours are proven here that the findings record alone cannot prove:
#   (B1) a pin the OLD auditor could never see - a path that exists ONLY inside a decoded
#        payload - is DETECTED AS BROKEN when it points nowhere, counted in broken_pins, and
#        still does not make the auditor exit nonzero (the reporting contract);
#   (B2) --expect-pins is the only opt-in nonzero path: it fires on a mismatch and stays 0
#        on a match, so a caller can gate on the pin count without the auditor gating itself;
#   (B3) a non-canonical base64 chunk (dirty padding bits - the shape a hand-mangled payload
#        takes) produces a VISIBLE note and exit 0, never a traceback and never a silent skip.
# Counts are RE-DERIVED from each fixture, never hardcoded, so this fence reads the same
# before and after t105's re-premise lands on the branch.
test -f docs/tools/leg_path_pin_audit.py || { echo "ac3 RED: the auditor is missing - run this fence from the repository root"; exit 1; }
test -f docs/state/merge_test_index.json || { echo "ac3 RED: index missing"; exit 1; }
command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "ac3 RED: python3 is missing"; exit 1; }
TMP=$(mktemp -d) || { echo "ac3 RED: mktemp -d failed"; exit 1; }
export TMP
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT INT TERM
python3 - <<'PYAC3' || exit 1
import base64, hashlib, json, os, re, subprocess, sys
IDX = "docs/state/merge_test_index.json"
TOOL = "docs/tools/leg_path_pin_audit.py"
TMP = os.environ["TMP"]
CHUNK = re.compile(r"(?<![A-Za-z0-9+/=])([A-Za-z0-9+/]{80,}={0,2})(?![A-Za-z0-9+/=])")
PIN_RE = re.compile(r"^leg_path_pin_audit: pin leg (\d+) issue=(\S+) ac=(\S+) path=(\S+) status=(\S+) via=(\S+)")
def fail(m):
    sys.stderr.write("ac3 RED: " + m + "\n"); raise SystemExit(1)
raw = open(IDX, "rb").read().replace(b"\r\n", b"\n")
idx = json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))
legs = idx["tests"]
# This fence MUTATES index JSON in memory, so it carries its own guard: the tracked index
# must be byte-identical at the end of the run. The mutations below only ever write copies
# into the throwaway dir, and this card carries ZERO index bytes - the guard makes that
# claim checkable inside the fence that comes closest to breaking it.
GUARD = hashlib.sha256(open(IDX, "rb").read()).hexdigest()
def run(tool_args):
    p = subprocess.run(["python3", TOOL] + tool_args, capture_output=True, text=True)
    return p.returncode, (p.stdout or "").replace("\r\n", b"\n".decode()).strip("\n"), (p.stderr or "").strip()
def pinlines(out):
    got = []
    for ln in out.split("\n"):
        m = PIN_RE.match(ln)
        if m:
            got.append((int(m.group(1)), m.group(2), m.group(3), m.group(4), m.group(5), m.group(6)))
    return got
# ---------- B1: planted broken pin inside a payload ----------
# Leg 315 (t88 ac1) is one of the 11 hidden legs. Its payload names its own card, in the
# live form before t105 and the closed/ form after; the regex covers BOTH shapes so this
# fixture is the same mutation on either side of the re-premise. The planted path points at
# a card that exists in NO location, so the correct report is missing_everywhere + a bumped
# broken_pins + exit 0.
LEG = 315
ISSUE = legs[LEG]["issue_id"]
ANCH = re.compile(r"docs/issues/(?:closed/)?%s\.md" % ISSUE)
FAKE = "docs/issues/closed/t9001.md"
cmd = legs[LEG]["command"]
ms = list(CHUNK.finditer(cmd))
planted = None
for k, m in enumerate(ms):
    try:
        pay = base64.b64decode(m.group(1)).decode("utf-8")
    except Exception:
        continue
    if ANCH.search(pay):
        new_pay = ANCH.sub(FAKE, pay, count=1)
        new_chunk = base64.b64encode(new_pay.encode("utf-8")).decode("ascii")
        legs[LEG]["command"] = cmd[:m.start()] + new_chunk + cmd[m.end():]
        planted = k
        break
if planted is None:
    fail("leg %d (%s) carries no payload naming its own card in either the live or the closed/ form - the hidden-leg shape this fence mutates is not present; re-groom against the index that exists" % (LEG, ISSUE))
fx1 = os.path.join(TMP, "index_planted.json")
open(fx1, "w", newline="\n").write(json.dumps(idx, indent=2))
rc, out, err = run(["--index", fx1])
if rc != 0:
    fail("B1 contract: the auditor exited %d on a parseable fixture with a broken pin in it (stderr: %s) - an AUDIT reports by printing and exits 0 whenever the index loads; only --expect-pins may return 1" % (rc, err[:140]))
got = pinlines(out)
hit = [g for g in got if g[0] == LEG and g[3] == FAKE]
if not hit:
    fail("B1 BITE MISSING: leg %d's payload was made to name %s (a card that exists in no location) and the auditor printed no pin line for it - a decode view that cannot see a planted broken pin cannot be trusted to see a real one, and this is the exact failure mode (WAL 1236) that made 11 archival breaks invisible" % (LEG, FAKE))
if not all(g[4] == "missing_everywhere" for g in hit):
    fail("B1: the planted pin on leg %d classified %s, expected missing_everywhere - %s exists neither at the pinned path nor under closed/ nor groom/" % (LEG, sorted({g[4] for g in hit}), FAKE))
if not all(g[5] == "decoded_base64" for g in hit):
    fail("B1: the planted pin on leg %d came back via=%s, expected decoded_base64 - the pin exists ONLY inside the payload, so a plaintext attribution would be a lie about how it was found" % (LEG, sorted({g[5] for g in hit})))
m = re.search(r"^leg_path_pin_audit: broken_pins=(\d+)$", out, re.M)
if not m:
    fail("B1: no broken_pins summary line (exact format) on the planted fixture")
broken_planted = int(m.group(1))
rc0, out0, _ = run(["--index", IDX])
m0 = re.search(r"^leg_path_pin_audit: broken_pins=(\d+)$", out0, re.M)
if not m0:
    fail("B1: no broken_pins summary line when run against the tracked index - the same contract must hold on both runs")
base_broken = int(m0.group(1))
if broken_planted != base_broken + 1:
    fail("B1: broken_pins moved from %d (tracked index) to %d (planted fixture), expected exactly +1 - the planted pin must be COUNTED, not merely printed; a view that prints but does not count leaves every consumer's broken-pin gate blind" % (base_broken, broken_planted))
print("ac3 evidence: B1 - planted %s inside leg %d's decoded payload: reported as missing_everywhere via=decoded_base64, broken_pins %d -> %d, auditor still exit 0" % (FAKE, LEG, base_broken, broken_planted))
# ---------- B2: --expect-pins is the only nonzero path, and it fires both ways ----------
mp = re.search(r"^leg_path_pin_audit: pinned_legs=(\d+)$", out, re.M)
if not mp:
    fail("B2: no pinned_legs summary line on the planted fixture")
derived = int(mp.group(1))
rc, out, err = run(["--index", fx1, "--expect-pins", str(derived)])
if rc != 0:
    fail("B2: --expect-pins=%d against a fixture whose derived pinned_legs IS %d exited %d - the gate must be silent-0 on a match or it trains callers to ignore it" % (derived, derived, rc))
rc, out, err = run(["--index", fx1, "--expect-pins", str(derived + 1)])
if rc != 1:
    fail("B2: --expect-pins=%d against a fixture whose derived pinned_legs is %d exited %d, expected 1 - the gate is the ONLY opt-in nonzero path this auditor has, and a gate that never fires is decoration" % (derived + 1, derived, rc))
if "EXPECT-PINS GATE" not in out:
    fail("B2: the mismatch run exited 1 without printing the 'EXPECT-PINS GATE' line - a nonzero exit with no printed reason is unattributable in a CI log")
print("ac3 evidence: B2 - --expect-pins %d -> rc 0 (match), %d -> rc 1 with the gate line printed (derived pinned_legs=%d)" % (derived, derived + 1, derived))
# ---------- B3: non-canonical chunk is noted, not crashed on ----------
# Only the LAST character of a padded base64 group carries unused bits: position -3 for a
# '==' group (two-pad, 4 unused bits) and position -2 for a '=' group (one-pad, 2 unused
# bits). Flipping one bit THERE leaves b64decode's OUTPUT identical while making the
# re-encode differ - the measurable definition of non-canonical, and the shape a hand-edited
# payload takes. (Flipping the character just BEFORE the padding instead changes a real data
# bit and re-encodes cleanly; that dead end was measured at groom, and it is why this
# construction is written out rather than assumed.)
ALPHABET = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/"
def dirtify(c):
    if c.endswith("=="):
        pos = len(c) - 3
    elif c.endswith("="):
        pos = len(c) - 2
    else:
        return None
    try:
        val = ALPHABET.index(c[pos])
    except ValueError:
        return None
    return c[:pos] + ALPHABET[val ^ 1] + c[pos + 1:]
dirty_leg = None
for i, leg in enumerate(legs):
    cmd = leg["command"]
    for m2 in CHUNK.finditer(cmd):
        c = m2.group(1)
        dirty = dirtify(c)
        if dirty is None or dirty == c:
            continue
        try:
            a = base64.b64decode(c)
            b = base64.b64decode(dirty)
        except Exception:
            continue
        if a != b:
            continue  # must be a pure padding-bit flip: identical decoded bytes
        if base64.b64encode(b).decode("ascii") != dirty:
            legs[i]["command"] = cmd.replace(c, dirty, 1)
            dirty_leg = i
            break
    if dirty_leg is not None:
        break

if dirty_leg is None:
    fail("B3: no padded chunk could be made non-canonical by a padding-bit flip - the non-canonical shape cannot be constructed from this index; re-groom rather than skip")
fx3 = os.path.join(TMP, "index_noncanonical.json")
open(fx3, "w", newline="\n").write(json.dumps(idx, indent=2))
rc, out, err = run(["--index", fx3])
if rc != 0:
    fail("B3: the auditor exited %d on a fixture carrying a non-canonical chunk (stderr: %s) - the contract is a VISIBLE note and exit 0: a hand-mangled payload must not turn the auditor into a traceback, and must not be silently skipped either" % (rc, err[:200]))
if "non-canonical" not in out.lower():
    fail("B3: leg %d's chunk was made non-canonical (decodes, but re-encode differs) and the auditor printed no 'non-canonical' note - silent acceptance of a hand-mangled chunk is how a doctored payload hides inside an audit that exists to catch doctored payloads" % dirty_leg)
if re.search(r"leg %d\b" % dirty_leg, out) is None and str(dirty_leg) not in out:
    fail("B3: the non-canonical note does not name the leg (%d) carrying the dirty chunk - an unattributed note cannot be acted on" % dirty_leg)
print("ac3 evidence: B3 - dirty padding bits planted in leg %d's chunk: auditor printed a non-canonical note naming the leg and exited 0" % dirty_leg)
if hashlib.sha256(open(IDX, "rb").read()).hexdigest() != GUARD:
    fail("SELF-GUARD: %s changed while this fence ran - every mutation here is supposed to land on a COPY under the throwaway dir, and this card carries zero index bytes; an in-memory json mutation that leaked to disk would be the exact violation t105's amendment exists to fence off" % IDX)
print("ac3 GREEN: THE CHECKER BITES - a payload-only broken pin is detected, classified missing_everywhere via=decoded_base64 and counted (+1 broken_pins) with exit 0; --expect-pins is the only nonzero path and fires in both directions; a non-canonical chunk yields a visible attributed note, never a crash or a silent skip")
PYAC3

set -u
# ac6 - PURITY + REPRODUCIBILITY against the BRANCH BASE, DERIVED AT RUN TIME.
# Read-only. The base comes from the BRANCH SHAPE, never from a main-tip-at-groom literal:
# the groom-INGEST commit (this card + the groom handoff + one WAL line) always sits between
# the groom-time main tip and any base a builder can legally hold, so a pinned tip drags
# docs/log/orchestrator_wal.jsonl - a path the builder must NEVER touch - into a delta nobody
# can remove. That was t102's structurally un-greenable ac6 (WAL 1221/1222). The WAL is
# deliberately NOT in ALLOWED: it sits BELOW the branch base, so if it ever appears inside a
# branch delta, RED is right.
# The frozen-neighbour list LEADS WITH THE INDEX: this card carries ZERO index bytes because
# the written ownership amendment belongs to t105 and to t105 alone, and the two cards are
# parallel-safe only if each one freezes the other's surface. Nothing is quoted: the ac_hash
# is RECOMPUTED from the shipped card.
test -f docs/issues/t106.md || { echo "ac6 RED: this card is missing - run from the repository root"; exit 1; }
command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "ac6 RED: python3 missing"; exit 1; }

import hashlib, json, os, re, subprocess, sys
CARD = "docs/issues/t106.md"
GROOM = "docs/state/outputs/t106_definer_groom.json"
# The builder handoff is named explicitly (the t102 amendment lesson): the card's Definition
# of Done requires it ON THE BRANCH, so it is part of the card's named surface. ONE literal
# path - no glob, no directory, and NOT docs/log/orchestrator_wal.jsonl (see the header).
BUILDER = "docs/state/outputs/t106_builder_build.json"
# The DELIVERABLES (the product) arrive on the builder branch. Base rejection below tests
# these, never the card or the groom handoff: both ride the groom-ingest commit, which always
# sits between the base and the product, so testing them would reject the branch parent.
DELIVERABLES = ["docs/tools/leg_path_pin_audit.py",
                "docs/state/outputs/t106_checker_b64_findings.json"]
# t105's whole surface is frozen HERE (index, decision record, card), which is what makes the
# two cards parallel-safe: neither can reach the other's bytes. The sibling surface is split
# from the always-present neighbours because t105's decision record legitimately DOES NOT
# EXIST until t105's builder lands: absent at the base AND absent in the tree is the pre-t105
# state (disclosed, not failure), present in the tree while absent at the base means index or
# t105 bytes arrived on THIS card's branch (RED), and a file that existed at the base but is
# gone from the tree is loss (RED).
SIBLING_SURFACE = ["docs/state/merge_test_index.json",
                   "docs/state/outputs/t105_repremise_decisions.json",
                   "docs/issues/t105.md"]
FROZEN_NEIGHBOURS = ["docs/state/outputs/t104_hygiene_findings.json",
                     "README.md", "openapi.yaml", "docs/requirements.md",
                     "docs/criteria/agent_pack_verification.md",
                     "docs/criteria/req_coverage_verification.md",
                     "docs/criteria/docs_verification.md", "docs/criteria/dashboard_verification.md",
                     "docs/criteria/infra_verification.md",
                     "docs/criteria/security_ops_verification.md",
                     "docs/plan.md", "docs/backlog.md", "docs/state/dag.json",
                     "docs/state/dag.mmd", "docs/state/issue_map.json",
                     "docs/state/merge_history.json", "docs/issues/t78.md"]
KEYS = ("GIT_DIR", "GIT_WORK_TREE", "GIT_INDEX_FILE", "GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY",
        "GIT_COMMON_DIR", "GIT_PREFIX")
def fail(m):
    sys.stderr.write("ac6 RED: " + m + "\n"); raise SystemExit(1)
def cr(b):
    return b.replace(b"\r\n", b"\n")
def env():
    return {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if k not in KEYS}
def git(args):
    p = subprocess.run(["git"] + args, capture_output=True, env=env())
    return cr(p.stdout or b""), (p.stderr or b"").decode("utf-8", "replace"), p.returncode
def blob(rev_, path):
    out, err, _ = git(["show", "%s:%s" % (rev_, path)])
    if not out:
        w = subprocess.run(["wslpath", "-w", os.getcwd()], capture_output=True,
                           text=True, env=env()).stdout.strip().replace("\r\n", "\n")
        out, err, _ = git(["cmd.exe", "/d", "/c", "git -C %s show %s:%s" % (w, rev_, path)])
    if not out:
        fail("blob %s:%s unreadable through WSL git AND cmd.exe git (%s)" % (rev_, path, err[:120]))
    return out
def rev(spec):
    out, _, rc = git(["rev-parse", "--revs-only", spec])
    r = out.decode("utf-8", "replace").strip()
    return r if rc == 0 and r else ""
def merge_base(ref):
    if not rev(ref):
        return ""
    out, _, rc = git(["merge-base", ref, "HEAD"])
    b = out.decode("utf-8", "replace").strip()
    return b if rc == 0 and b else ""
def blob_at(rev_, path):
    probe, _, rc = git(["rev-parse", "--verify", "-q", "%s:%s" % (rev_, path)])
    if rc != 0 or not probe.strip():
        return None
    return blob(rev_, path)
def rejection(cand):
    if not cand:
        return "unresolvable on this checkout"
    if cand == rev("HEAD"):
        return "is HEAD itself, not a base"
    _, _, rc = git(["merge-base", "--is-ancestor", cand, "HEAD"])
    if rc != 0:
        return "is not an ancestor of HEAD"
    for p in DELIVERABLES:
        try:
            w = cr(open(p, "rb").read())
        except OSError:
            return "%s is missing from this tree" % p
        at = blob_at(cand, p)
        if at is not None and at == w:
            return "%s already equals its blob there - that commit carries the PRODUCT, so diffing against it would make the purity check vacuous (the card and the groom handoff are NOT rejection material: they ride the groom-ingest commit, which always sits between the base and the product)" % p
    return ""
CANDIDATES = [("HEAD^ (the branch parent)", rev("HEAD^")),
              ("merge-base(main, HEAD)", merge_base("main")),
              ("merge-base(origin/main, HEAD)", merge_base("origin/main"))]
BASE = BASE_LABEL = ""
for label, cand in CANDIDATES:
    if BASE:
        print("ac6 evidence: base candidate %s -> %s not tested (the base is already resolved)" % (label, cand[:7] or "(none)"))
        continue
    why = rejection(cand)
    if why:
        print("ac6 evidence: base candidate %s -> %s rejected: %s" % (label, cand[:7] or "(none)", why))
    else:
        BASE, BASE_LABEL = cand, label
        print("ac6 evidence: base candidate %s -> %s ACCEPTED (strict pre-product ancestor of HEAD)" % (label, cand[:7]))
if not BASE:
    fail("no candidate base (%s) is a strict pre-product ancestor of HEAD - the branch is not in the (base -> product -> handoff) shape this card assumes, so the purity base cannot be derived; name the branch shape and re-groom rather than pin a literal" % ", ".join(l for l, _ in CANDIDATES))
print("ac6 evidence: PURITY BASE = %s derived from %s - the groom-INGEST commit sits BELOW this base, which is why docs/log/orchestrator_wal.jsonl cannot legitimately appear in this delta and is deliberately NOT in ALLOWED" % (BASE[:7], BASE_LABEL))
def names(args):
    out, err, rc = git(args)
    if rc != 0:
        fail("git %s failed: %s" % (" ".join(args), err[:160]))
    return [p for p in out.decode("utf-8", "replace").split("\n") if p.strip()]
tracked_delta = sorted(set(names(["diff", "--name-only", BASE])
                           + names(["diff", "--name-only", "--cached", BASE])))
ALLOWED = set(DELIVERABLES + [CARD, GROOM, BUILDER])
extra = sorted(set(tracked_delta) - ALLOWED)
if extra:
    fail("the delta touches %s beyond the two deliverables (the upgraded auditor, the findings record), this card and the two handoffs the Definition of Done requires - this card carries ZERO index bytes and ZERO t105 bytes, and every extra path here is outside that boundary" % ", ".join(extra))
print("ac6 evidence: delta against %s is exactly: %s" % (BASE[:7], ", ".join(tracked_delta) if tracked_delta else "(nothing)"))
POLLUTION_ROOTS = ("scratch", "build", "node_modules", ".venv", ".pytest_cache",
                   ".pi-agent", "__pycache__")
untracked = names(["ls-files", "--others", "--exclude-standard"])
strays, exc = [], []
for p in untracked:
    if any(root in p.split("/") for root in POLLUTION_ROOTS) or p.endswith(".pyc"):
        exc.append(p)
    elif p.startswith("docs/state/") and not p.endswith(".md"):
        exc.append(p)  # orchestrator bookkeeping and later-phase handoffs
    elif p not in ALLOWED:
        strays.append(p)
if strays:
    fail("untracked paths sit outside the owned surface and outside the two named exception classes (session pollution roots; pre-existing non-markdown artifacts under docs/state/): %s" % ", ".join(sorted(strays)[:12]))
print("ac6 evidence: untracked screen - %d pollution-root paths, %d pre-existing docs/state/ artifacts, zero strays" % (len(exc), len([p for p in exc if p.startswith("docs/state/")])))
missing = [p for p in DELIVERABLES if not os.path.isfile(p)]
if missing:
    fail("%s missing from the tree - the deliverables must all be present, whether they rode the ingest commit or arrived on this branch" % ", ".join(missing))
def frozen(path, why):
    at = blob_at(BASE, path)
    if at is None:
        fail("%s does not exist at the derived base %s - it is a frozen neighbour and must predate this card (%s)" % (path, BASE[:7], why))
    if not os.path.isfile(path):
        fail("%s vanished from the tree while it exists at %s (%s)" % (path, BASE[:7], why))
    b, w = cr(at), cr(open(path, "rb").read())
    if b != w:
        fail("%s differs from its %s blob (base %s vs work %s) - %s" % (path, BASE[:7], hashlib.sha256(b).hexdigest()[:12], hashlib.sha256(w).hexdigest()[:12], why))
    return True
SIB_FREEZE = "the INDEX and t105's decision record and card are FROZEN for this card: the written ownership amendment names t105 ONLY and this card carries ZERO index bytes"
NEIGH_FREEZE = "README, openapi, requirements, the six criteria documents, the t104 findings record, the bookkeeping and the t78 exemption are FROZEN for this card"
present_sibling = 0
for p in SIBLING_SURFACE:
    at_base = blob_at(BASE, p) is not None
    in_tree = os.path.isfile(p)
    if not at_base and not in_tree:
        print("ac6 evidence: sibling surface %s absent at the base and in the tree - t105 has not landed yet on this branch, which is a legitimate pre-t105 state and NOT a violation (this card must not require the sibling's product)" % p)
        continue
    if at_base and not in_tree:
        fail("%s existed at the base %s but is gone from the tree - %s" % (p, BASE[:7], SIB_FREEZE))
    if in_tree and not at_base:
        fail("%s appears in the tree but not at the base %s - t105's product (or an index edit) has arrived on THIS card's branch, and this card's delta is supposed to hold zero bytes of it" % (p, BASE[:7]))
    frozen(p, SIB_FREEZE)
    present_sibling += 1
for p in FROZEN_NEIGHBOURS:
    frozen(p, NEIGH_FREEZE)
print("ac6 evidence: %d frozen neighbours byte-identical to their %s blobs, plus %d of 3 t105-surface paths frozen (the rest are legitimately not yet created)" % (len(FROZEN_NEIGHBOURS), BASE[:7], present_sibling))
card = cr(open(CARD, "rb").read()).decode("utf-8")
blocks = re.findall(r"(?ms)^### (ac\d+) - .*?^```bash\n(.*?)^```\n", card)
if not blocks:
    fail("no fenced bash blocks found in the shipped card - the ac_hash cannot be recomputed, which means the card's fences were not shipped as groomed")
ids = [b[0] for b in blocks]
if len(blocks) != 6 or ids != ["ac1", "ac2", "ac3", "ac4", "ac5", "ac6"]:
    fail("the shipped card carries %d fences %s, not the six in ac1..ac6 order - the ac_hash is defined over exactly six fenced blocks in order" % (len(blocks), ids))
bodies = [b[1].replace("\r", "").strip() for b in blocks]
digest = hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(bodies, separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
print("ac6 evidence: recomputed ac_hash from the shipped fences = %s (t58 recipe: sha256 over the JSON array of the six fenced bash bodies, COMPACT separators, each CR-stripped and trimmed)" % digest)
if not os.path.isfile(GROOM):
    fail("%s missing - the ac_hash cannot be cross-checked and Gate 1 has nothing to read" % GROOM)
if not os.path.isfile(BUILDER):
    fail("%s is NOT on this branch - the Definition of Done requires the builder handoff alongside the product, and ac6 names it in ALLOWED precisely so the branch is checked for it (the t102 amendment lesson: name the required handoff artifacts, then look for them)" % BUILDER)
h = json.loads(cr(open(GROOM, "rb").read()).decode("utf-8"))
